| [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | Roles in disjoint contexts cannot conflict | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. So "tall", which takes one threshold for people and another for trees, is one global section with the comparison class part of the meaning, not a failure of gluing. A failure needs contexts that overlap and carry sections that disagree there. Which families count as covering is the piece that decides whether anything glues, and a sheaf picture of meaning that does not state it has decided nothing. | Active |

The two answer different questions, "is it there?" and "can it be reached in time?", and come apart in both directions. MOM's table was re-run here and reproduced, and a simulation of the search agrees. | Active |
| [CLAIM-309](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md) | Mixture quality is not discriminability | The smoothie note in the owner's LEGO monograph reads the owner's line ([CASE-096](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md)) as signal detection. Milk is the noise, "Less Good" is d′ falling as the mixture approaches milk, and "More Good" is d′ rising as a little milk is added. Under linear mixing the mixture's taste is (1 − f)s + f·m, and its distance from milk is (1 − f)\|s − m\|. That falls monotonically from the first drop, so discriminability from milk cannot rise and then fall. The note's own first model is right: goodness is a single-peaked function of the ratio, which is a preference, not a discriminability. Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Applied to the undamped oscillator switching ω between 0.5 and 3 every unit of time: λ = 0.1955, and with δ = 0.1 the system is stable at every instant, with eigenvalues −0.1 ± 3i and −0.1 ± 0.5i, and has exponent 0.0955. | Active |

Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |

If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |

And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |

Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. Then a constant kernel fits only target responses that carry no information about the item. An exact fit is a garbling, with the item as the common parameter. And Le Cam's deficiency between the two finite tables is one linear programme. Its restriction to finitely many decision problems is a finite computation. It does not say the measure is informative, which is [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s empirical question. | Active |
| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) v2 | Autoencoder representations are rotation-invariant | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. The sharp constants, and that the growth is no more than order R, come from the computation and are not here. | Active |

| [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v6 | A legibility state adds a mode to the loop | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. On Frijda's account an emotion is an appraisal of an event's pertinence to a concern, eliciting action readiness with control precedence; a corporation has concerns, appraisals and readiness. A harm to others reaches its decisions either as one of its own concerns (procedures, role duties: functional concern and remorse) or as a threat to its other concerns (regulators, markets: functional fear). Take configurations joined by reversible moves, each move with a peak requirement, and let d(x, y) be the least, over paths, of the largest requirement on the path ([CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md)'s threshold, identities free). Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). Under additive costs d is a metric and budgeted identification is intransitive in general. So which resource semantics governs a system decides whether "the same thing, within budget" sorts its configurations into a hierarchy of kinds at all. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

Implication does not remove the linear directions. Every attribute is read out exactly, by an affine map, from the full-rank spectral embedding, and the recovered incidence and its concept lattice equal the generating ones. What implication changes is the spectrum. On a balanced b-ary tree, the eigenvectors are branch contrasts rather than one per attribute. A branching at depth ℓ gives eigenvalue μ_ℓ = w Σ_{ℓ′>ℓ} λ_ℓ′ b^(D−ℓ′), with multiplicity (b−1)bˡ, and these fall strictly with depth for any positive strengths. So a rank-(b^K − 1) embedding reads out exactly the attributes of depth at most K. Below the cut, each attribute's readout is the same constant on every descendant of its depth-K ancestor, so siblings merge. Along a tree, PMI additivity is therefore the same thing as piecewise constancy on the finest groups: it has content only where attributes cross-cut, as in analogy families. For fixed configurations Ω and fixed response laws, let π(Q) be the partition of Ω into classes no probe in Q separates. Then π(Q1 ∪ Q2) is the meet (common refinement) of π(Q1) and π(Q2), while π(Q1 ∩ Q2) is at least as coarse as their join and can be strictly coarser. So π is order-reversing and meet-preserving, its image is a meet-closed part of the partition lattice and need not be a sublattice, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members, against Bell(\|Ω\|) partitions (32 against 115,975 for m = 5 and \|Ω\| = 10). Checked with python3 -I on 3,000 random probe systems (no union failed; the intersection was strictly coarser than the join in 100) and on an explicit case. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
